headline: Light rain and snow wind down Sunday night, Monday into Tuesday afternoon is the best window for holiday travel through the mountains, a weaker storm brings light snow Tuesday night or Wednesday, and Thanksgiving looks dry and mild.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A weak Pacific storm brings periods of light rain and snow through Sunday evening before showers clear out later tonight, with only minor travel impacts in the Sierra. Snow totals are meager: up to 2 inches along the Sierra crest, especially around the Tahoe Basin, with a 10 percent chance of 2 to 4 inches on the highest peaks by Monday morning; elsewhere, including the Mammoth Lakes area, expect a trace to an inch under heavier snow showers. Valley floors see a rain-snow mix with, at most, a trace on grass or elevated surfaces, and Reno has a 20 to 30 percent chance of a light rain-snow mix between about 2 and 6 PM. As skies clear tonight, pockets of freezing fog may form in northeast California and eastern Sierra valleys into early Monday, with low clouds and patchy fog possible in Reno and the Carson Valley.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: High pressure brings a dry break Monday into Tuesday afternoon, the best window for holiday travel through the mountains. Winds pick up Tuesday ahead of the next storm, with southwest gusts of 25 to 35 mph near the Oregon border and across eastern Sierra valleys and ridgetop gusts up to 80 mph at times, affecting backcountry and lake recreation and making for bumpy flights. The next storm, which has trended much weaker, arrives Tuesday night into Wednesday: there is a 70 percent chance of 2 to 3 inches along the Sierra crest, a 70 to 90 percent chance of 1 to 2 inches at pass level, and a 60 to 90 percent chance of at least a trace at Truckee and lake level and along and west of US-395 in Mono County, including Mammoth Lakes. Snow levels rise from 5,000–5,500 feet to near 7,000 feet during the storm, so snow should switch to rain below the Sierra passes sometime Wednesday, while western Nevada valleys likely see only rain, if showers make it past the mountains at all (10 percent chance of light valley snow Wednesday morning).

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A quick disturbance passing to the north brings low shower chances near the Oregon border on Thanksgiving Day; otherwise Thanksgiving and the Friday after are expected to be dry and mild. Unsettled weather looks likely to close out November and start December, with another storm possible next weekend (November 28–29).

watch_for: Freezing fog in eastern Sierra valleys and around Truckee tonight into early Monday.
Gusty winds Tuesday (25–35 mph in valleys, up to 80 mph on ridgetops) and light mountain snow Tuesday night into Wednesday during busy holiday travel.
Another possible storm next weekend, November 28–29.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in light snow totals with today's storm and a dry Monday–Tuesday break, note the midweek storm has trended much weaker with some uncertainty about how far showers reach into western Nevada, and favor a dry, mild Thanksgiving with storms possible again next weekend.
